page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-192-lssd is a compute-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 192 dedicated virtual CPUs, representing 96 physical cores with hyper-threading, operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. The processor is supported by a 504 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 720 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 3.75 GB per core. Local storage is bundled directly, providing 12,599 GB of NVMe SSD capacity across 32 local drives.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and Passmark CPU scores ranking in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, achieving top-tier ratings for both cached small-block and uncached large-block read operations. While single-core stress-ng performance falls into the average category, the server excels in parallelized tasks, showing top-tier results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, software compilation, and database operations.

There is a performance variance in LLM inference workloads; prompt processing speeds for small, medium, and large models rank as strong, whereas text generation speeds drop to average. This makes the server highly effective for high-throughput database operations, static web serving, and parallelized compilation tasks, but less optimal for workloads requiring high single-core performance or GPU-accelerated deep learning. The high density of local NVMe SSD storage combined with top-tier Redis SET operations makes it well-suited for large-scale caching and high-IOPS database deployments.
